title: 分散システム
subtitle: Distributed Object Oriented Systems
educationalGoal: A distributed system is a technology for integrating both computers and networks. Currently, many distributed systems have been formed from many technologies. Although I can't explain them all in this course, I will systematically explain as many as I can in the limited time of 15 weeks.
advice: This is application course of computer network within which we will cover the following materials: 1. Network Architecture 2. Client&Server Model 3. Computer Communication (Remote Procedure Call) 4. Synchronization 5. Replication and Consistency 6. Fault Torrance 7. Network Security Students are expected to understand the mechanisms of network computing (include cluster computing). At the end of each chapter, some quizzes are attached so that the student's level of understanding can be confirmed. In addition, I will recommend related materials (books and URLs) that are suitable for furthering student understanding.
requiredKnowledge: The units of “Programming 3” and “Information Network” are expected to have been acquired. Attendance is completely unrelated to student evaluations. However, if students do not attend at least two-thirds of the whole course, they will not be eligible to take the achievement confirmation test. Instead of covering all the contents described in the textbooks, we will select and explain as necessary. Then, after each commentary, students will have group work to solve presented problems and will give a presentation at the beginning of the next class.

achievementLevels.ideal: Explain distributed systems. The following elemental technologies required for distributed systems can be learned, and concrete technical contents can be explained: 1. Network architecture 2. Client-server model 3. Computer communication (remote procedure call) 4. Synchronization 5. Replication and consistency 6. Fault Torrance 7. Network security
achievementLevels.standard: Understand distributed systems. The following multiple elemental technologies required for a distributed system can be learned, and technical contents at the word level can be explained: 1. Network architecture 2. Client-server model 3. Computer communication (remote procedure call) 4. Synchronization 5. Replication and consistency 6. Fault Torrance 7. Network security

lessons.content: 1. Overview of distributed systems I will take up what a distributed system is and explain some of its advantages over a centralized system.
2. Types of distributed systems Understand the types and purposes of distributed systems. Learn what is different about how each type of configuration.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 2 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 3 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 3. Architecture Learn basic design and concepts such as the design philosophy and basic design of distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 3 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 4 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 4. Process Learn about the execution units in a distributed system such as “process” and “thread”.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 4 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 5 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 5. Client-Server model Learn the classification and characteristics of both clients and servers from several perspectives.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 5 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 6 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 6. Communication Learn about basic reference models and basic functions for exchanging data between components of a distributed system.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 6 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 7 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 7. Naming Explain common naming issues in distributed systems and learn about the main methods of naming.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 7 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 8 of the textbook)

lessons.content: - Mid-term exam 8. Synchronization Learn about the basic methods of clock synchronization and the exclusive control algorithms in distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 8 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 9 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 9. Replication and Consistency Learn about replication and consistency models for improved reliability and performance.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 9 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 10 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 10. Fault Torrent Learn about basic concepts and techniques for introducing fault tolerance into distributed systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 10 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 11 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 11. Network Security Learn about cryptographic technologies, authentication technologies, communication methods, and access control.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 11 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 12 of the textbook)

lessons.content: 12. Distributed files and objects Learn the advantages and disadvantages of distributed files compared to centralized file systems.
lessons.assignments: Review (Chapter 12 of Textbook) Preparation (Chapter 13 of the textbook)

lessons.content: Hold a lecture on distributed systems with external lecturers.
